sections.title: What GuildAtlas is
sections.body: GuildAtlas is a directory where people discover Discord bots and Discord servers (discover discord bots and servers). Anyone can browse, search, filter, sort and open detail pages. Signing in with Discord is needed to submit a listing or see a dashboard.

sections.title: Signing in
sections.body: Login uses Discord OAuth with the identify and guilds scopes. The site does not store Discord access tokens. Signing in lets the site know which servers you manage so you can submit them.

sections.title: Submitting a bot
sections.body: Submit the bot's Application ID (17 to 20 digits). The site checks the Application ID with Discord and takes the name and icon from Discord. You must provide an invite link, a short description (20 to 140 characters), a full description (50 to 4000 characters), a category and a language, and confirm you own or are authorized to list the bot. Bot ownership is a confirmation checkbox; Discord offers no simple ownership check. A bot can be listed only once. Categories: moderation, music, utility, fun, games, economy, social, ai, logging, other.

sections.title: Submitting a server
sections.body: You must manage the server (Manage Server or Administrator, or be the owner) and the GuildAtlas bot must already be in that server. If the site cannot verify the bot is in the server, the submission is blocked; try again later or add the bot first. A server can be listed only once. Categories: community, gaming, development, education, art, music, anime, support, other.

sections.title: Listing statuses
sections.body:
- pending: Submitted and waiting for a reviewer. Not public.
- approved: Reviewed and public in the directory.
- changes_requested: A reviewer asked for changes. Not public. The owner sees the reviewer note on their dashboard.
- rejected: Not accepted. Not public. The owner sees the reviewer note on their dashboard.
- suspended: Previously approved, now hidden by a moderator. Not public.
Only approved listings are public. New listings always start as pending.

sections.title: How review works
sections.body:
Reviewers are trusted people configured by the site owner. Allowed actions and transitions:
- approve: from pending to approved
- reject: from pending or changes_requested to rejected (reviewer must give a reason)
- request changes: from pending to changes_requested (reviewer must give a reason)
- suspend: from approved to suspended (reviewer must give a reason)
- restore: from suspended to approved
Every action is recorded in an append-only audit log. Review notifications go to a private reviewer channel; reviewers act on the website or with buttons there, and the site re-verifies the reviewer each time. Submitted bots are never installed automatically. Reviewers who test a bot must do so in a controlled test server.

sections.title: Your dashboard
sections.body: The dashboard lists your own listings, their statuses and any reviewer note. You can only see your own listings.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.body:
- "Discord has no public application with this ID": check the Application ID in the Discord Developer Portal.
- "Could not verify with Discord": a temporary Discord problem; try again shortly.
- Server submission blocked: you must manage the server and the bot must be in it.
- "Already submitted": each bot and server can be listed once; contact support if it was not you.
- Listing not visible: it is probably still pending, or needs changes; check the dashboard.
- Cannot sign in: sign-in may not be configured yet.

sections.title: Not available yet
sections.body: These do NOT exist yet and must not be described as available: voting, user reviews and ratings, reports, analytics, API keys and the public API, webhooks, premium plans, boosts, donations and payments, editing or resubmitting a listing, and appeals. Do not invent dates or details for them.
